title: refactor: drop the read-through to the retired binary cache
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Every media cache miss fell through to `LEGACY_MEDIA_BUCKET`, the retired pre-migration binary cache. That kept a second, frozen key algorithm alive next to the real one, with both needing the same request-identity logic applied by hand. The file's own header said to delete it when the migration stopped being useful; no cutoff was ever set.

- Deletes `legacy-media-cache.ts`, its test, the `withLegacyMediaCache` wrapper and the `LEGACY_MEDIA_BUCKET` binding across all four wrangler environments
- Media cache adapters are now one plain object: one key algorithm, one bucket, no read-through
- 431 lines removed

### Notes

- The R2 bucket `pollinations-images` is untouched. Only the Worker binding goes, so this is reversible by re-adding it.
- That bucket is 25.6 TB over 221M objects and is pending archival to Glacier. The read-through was what required it to stay online.
- Objects that were never promoted stop being served and regenerate on next request.

gist.headline: One cache, fewer ghosts
gist.blurb: The media cache has stopped consulting its retired attic. New requests now follow one clean route to fresh pixels, and anything old that turns up gets regenerated.
gist.summary: Removed the retired `LEGACY_MEDIA_BUCKET` read-through from the gen worker, leaving media caching with one key algorithm and one active bucket instead of maintaining the frozen pre-migration path.
gist.impact: Media that was only stored in the old cache will regenerate on its next request, while the active `pollinations-images` R2 bucket and current cache behavior remain intact.

The scene represents removing a duplicate legacy lookup so generated media follows one clear path; a small monitor robot can happily point at the one active route.
